title: Complex Noun Phrases
completion_message: ¡Excelente! El uso de Frases Nominales (Noun Phrases) complejas es el secreto para redactar informes ejecutivos, artículos académicos y correos formales densos y profesionales, condensando información en pocas palabras.

parts.visual:
En inglés formal escrito (negocios/académico), se prefiere 'empaquetar' la información en frases nominales (Noun Phrases) en lugar de usar muchas oraciones con verbos. 
Ejemplo simple: The company grew rapidly. This surprised the investors. 
Ejemplo C1 (Noun Phrase): The company's RAPID GROWTH surprised the investors. 
Ejemplo simple: They developed a system to manage inventory. 
Ejemplo C1 (Noun Phrase): They developed an INVENTORY MANAGEMENT SYSTEM.
parts.audio: In formal written English, especially in business and academic contexts, it is common to pack information into complex Noun Phrases rather than using many clauses with verbs. Simple example: The company grew rapidly. This surprised the investors. C1 Noun Phrase equivalent: The company's RAPID GROWTH surprised the investors. We changed the verb 'grew' to the noun 'growth', and the adverb 'rapidly' to the adjective 'rapid'. Another simple example: They developed a system to manage inventory. C1 equivalent: They developed an INVENTORY MANAGEMENT SYSTEM.

parts.visual:
Técnicas de formación: 
1. Nouns as adjectives (Sustantivos como adjetivos): El modificador va en SINGULAR. 
Ej: A report of 50 pages -> A 50-PAGE report (no pages). 
Ej: A budget of two million dollars -> A TWO-MILLION-DOLLAR budget. 
2. Prepositional phrases (Frases preposicionales) para añadir detalle: 
Ej: The recent decline IN GLOBAL OIL PRICES has affected our margins. 
3. Nominalization (Convertir verbos en sustantivos): 
Ej: They failed to deliver. -> Their FAILURE to deliver caused problems.
parts.audio: Formation techniques. Number 1: Nouns as adjectives. Remember that the modifying noun must be in the SINGULAR form. Example: A report of 50 pages becomes a 50-PAGE report, not 'pages'. A budget of two million dollars becomes a TWO-MILLION-DOLLAR budget. Number 2: Prepositional phrases to add detail after the head noun. Example: The recent decline IN GLOBAL OIL PRICES has affected our margins. Number 3: Nominalization, which means turning verbs into nouns. Example: Instead of saying 'They failed to deliver', you say: Their FAILURE to deliver caused problems.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige la Noun Phrase correcta para lograr un estilo formal y conciso.

questions.question: Instead of 'The project took five years', use a noun phrase: It was a ____ project.
questions.explanation: Cuando un sustantivo con número actúa como adjetivo (antes de otro sustantivo), va en singular y con guion: five-year project.

questions.question: Instead of 'They invest a lot on a long term basis', use a noun phrase: They focus on ____.
questions.explanation: Long-term investment es una frase nominal formal.

questions.question: Convert the verb to a noun: 'They decided quickly, which saved us.' -> Their quick ____ saved us.
Instead of 'A contract of two million dollars', use: A ____ contract.
questions.explanation: Sustantivos como adjetivos siempre en singular: two-million-dollar.

questions.question: Instead of 'A policy for human resources', use: A ____ policy.
questions.explanation: Human resources es un caso especial donde 'resources' mantiene la 's' como parte del nombre del departamento (Human Resources policy), aunque 'human resource policy' también es aceptable a veces.

questions.question: Convert the verb to a noun: 'The CEO announced the merger, which surprised everyone.' -> The CEO's ____ of the merger surprised everyone.
Instead of 'A meeting that lasts two hours', use: A ____ meeting.
Convert the verb to a noun: 'They failed to reach an agreement.' -> Their ____ to reach an agreement was problematic.
Instead of 'We need to analyze the data completely', use: We need a complete ____ of the data.
questions.explanation: Nominalization: analyze -> analysis. Y el adverbio 'completely' pasa a ser adjetivo 'complete'.

questions.question: Instead of 'A hotel with five stars', use: A ____ hotel.
Convert 'They responded rapidly to the crisis' into a noun phrase: Their ____ to the crisis was impressive.
Instead of 'A plan that covers 10 points', use: A ____ plan.
Convert the verb: 'We intend to expand into Asia.' -> Our ____ to expand into Asia is clear.
questions.explanation: Nominalization: intend -> intention (o intent, pero intention es más común aquí).

questions.question: Instead of 'An approach focused on the customer', use: A ____ approach.
Convert 'The market grew significantly' into a noun phrase: The ____ in the market was unexpected.
Instead of 'A building with 50 stories', use: A ____ building.
Instead of 'A strategy to reduce costs', use: A ____ strategy.
Convert 'They evaluated the risk thoroughly': Their ____ of the risk was excellent.
Instead of 'An agreement for a joint venture', use: A ____ agreement.
Convert 'The team performed poorly' to a noun phrase: The team's ____ led to their dismissal.
